summary.headline: Ajmera Realty Q2 FY27 revenue rose 45% YoY to INR320 crore and PAT 55% to INR49 crore; debt cut to INR646 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 sales were INR224 crore (72,883 sq ft carpet) against collections of INR190 crore, and H1 sales reached INR370 crore. Revenue, EBITDA and PAT all grew strongly YoY, with 33Fifteen (Bandra commercial) recognising revenue for the first time this quarter. Debt fell INR34 crore QoQ to INR646 crore, debt-equity is 0.44x and weighted cost of debt dipped to 10.75%. Management's near-term story rests on about 8 launches (~38 lakh sq ft, ~INR7,000 crore top line) mostly in Q4 FY27, plus the Kanjurmarg 7-acre land conversion, which has slipped repeatedly and drew the most investor pushback.

financial_highlights.value: INR370 crore sales (1,16,620 sq ft) / INR363 crore collections
INR3,510 crore (INR1,550 crore committed sales + INR1,960 crore inventory to sell)
INR7,008 crore; total visibility above INR10,500 crore

segments.name: Mumbai residential and mixed-use projects
segments.commentary: Ajmera Manhattan 1 is 95% sold and possession is targeted next year. Greenfinity Phase 2 (Wadala) is 94%+ sold with OC expected within days. Vihara (Bhandup) is 84% sold and Solis Phase 1 is 87% sold, both still in excavation or foundation work.

segments.name: Commercial (33Fifteen, Bandra)
segments.commentary: 25% of inventory sold in the quarter, with excavation ongoing. Revenue recognition began this quarter on fast-track execution.

segments.name: Luxury (Vann by Ajmera, Versova)
segments.commentary: Only 4% sold, with shoring, piling and excavation underway. Management attributes the slow pace to micro-market competition and redevelopment supply, and says prices are not being cut.

segments.name: Bangalore mid-market
segments.commentary: Ajmera Iris is 94% sold with finishing underway and OC awaited. Ajmera Marina is 76% sold, with 8 of 21 slabs cast.

segments.name: Ajmera Manhattan 2 (Wadala)
segments.commentary: 56% of inventory sold; excavation done and raft works in progress.

guidance_outlook: About 8 launches in H2 FY27 (~38 lakh sq ft, ~INR7,000 crore top line): Solis early Dec or mid-Dec; Bangalore projects mid-Jan to Feb; Boutique office (Wadala) by mid-to-end Feb; Borivali and Whitefield by March; Vishrantwadi (Pune) first sales and TDR revenue by end March; Doddabalapur by Feb.
Management is confident of exceeding the INR2,200 crore presales target over the next six months, against INR370 crore in H1.
Wadala commercial (captive, annuity) to be built in two phases of about 10 lakh sq ft each; Phase 2 expected in FY28.
Management expects leverage headroom to roughly double from 0.44x to fund launches within the guided leverage range; financial closure reportedly in place for Wadala.
Estimated pre-tax cash flow post debt from ongoing and upcoming projects is about INR3,900 crore-plus over project life cycles.

Kanjurmarg 7-acre conversion: management hopes for conversion in this or the next quarter, possibly two quarters, but it is not guaranteed before 31 December. Conversion cost was earlier estimated at INR300-330 crore, and management declined to update the figure.
capex_capacity: Launch pipeline is about 8 projects, 38 lakh sq ft in total, spread across 8 micro-markets and multiple cities, so management sees limited internal cannibalisation.
Wadala commercial: 10 lakh sq ft at an estimated INR10,000/sq ft build cost (about INR1,000 crore per analyst's math), plus land conversion costs; the Phase 2 tower is of similar size and cost.
Ajmera Manhattan 1 is in MEP and finishing, with possession targeted next year. Solis and Vann are in early-stage excavation or piling.
Kanjurmarg 7-acre plot: the strategic partner route (monetisation, JV or funding) is still open; conversion is the gating item and the 55-acre master plan is largely frozen but not yet tied up.
demand_pricing: Management says Mumbai residential registrations are resilient and that premium homes above INR1 crore are a growing share of sales.
Commercial leasing is strong, led by GCC tenants, with Grade A office demand described as good.
RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps in its October policy. Management sees limited impact unless rates rise further.

Vann (Versova) pricing: competing stock is available at INR38,000, INR45,000 and INR50,000 per sq ft. Management is holding prices and expects sales to pick up when plinth and upper floors are visible.

Margins: management expects cost pressure from geopolitics and commodities to ease. It will time sales velocity and launches against cost and price elasticity. Analyst noted historic 30%+ EBITDA margins.

qa_highlights.question: Kanjurmarg 7-acre tie-up and conversion timing; will conversion happen before 31 Dec before cost rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says conversion is hoped for before 31 Dec but hurdles remain; it is a government process and it declined to quantify the cost if it slips. Commercial talks have not started, though title and approvals have progressed.

qa_highlights.question: Will presales of INR2,200 crore be met given the Q4 launch cluster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of exceeding the target within six months, citing 8 launches and early agent interest. It acknowledged up to one or two launches could slip because approvals are not fully in place.

qa_highlights.question: Balance sheet capacity to fund Wadala commercial plus launches within 6 to 9 months.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO says leverage is 0.44x with room to roughly double, financial closure is in place for Wadala, and Solis collections will accelerate cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Margin sustainability with cost inflation and pricing pressure.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects geopolitics and commodity pressure to normalise and will time launches and sales velocity against cost and pricing elasticity. No margin number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Kanjurmarg timeline visibility and what follows conversion.
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not commit to a timeline. After conversion it expects a 4-5 month routine master plan and approvals step, then a commercial and residential launch together and a 7-acre monetisation or JV.

qa_highlights.question: Vann sales slow and Kanjurmarg-style questions on water scarcity and BMC restrictions.
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed micro-market competition and redevelopment supply for Vann's slow sales. It said water shortages in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28 will be managed through tankers and borewells, and there are no BMC restrictions yet.

risks_watch: Kanjurmarg 7-acre conversion depends on government and court processes; the timeline has moved from June to December to 'next quarter or two', and the conversion cost may rise after 31 Dec.
Launch slippage: about 7 of 8 launches are concentrated in Q4 FY27, and approvals are not all in place.
Presales target of INR2,200 crore requires about INR1,830 crore in H2 against INR370 crore in H1.
Vann (Versova) has only 4% sold, and the management response is to hold prices.
Rate hike and affordability; cost inflation and margin pressure from labour and materials; Q4 and Q1 water shortage affecting construction pace.
Leverage will rise if the Wadala commercial build (about INR1,000 crore) and the Phase 2 tower run in parallel with the launch cluster.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and launches, but evasive on the Kanjurmarg conversion. Management repeatedly said it cannot give a timeline or a cost figure, and it deflected questions on Vann sales and the Wadala split of presales.
